newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 11.

text.p: There are 81 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The Beijing-backed TA KUNG PAO said Governor Chris Patten should not interfere in the public consultation process for the proposed changes to laws on societies and demonstrations. The British administration's opposition to the ban on funding of local societies by foreign political groups was aimed at introducing foreign political pressures into Hong Kong and changing it from an economic city into a political city.

-- The English-language HONG KONG STANDARD said the social order document was far too vague. The more one studied it the more loopholes one found, the paper said. The three week consultation period was probably not long enough and there were no alternatives offered, but there was no doubt that time was running short if the legislation was to be completed before the handover, it said.

-- The MING PAO DAILY said the Chinese and Hong Kong governments should announce as soon as possible a timetable for the intake of children from the mainland eligible to settle in the territory. But strict measures should be taken to curb illegal immigration, and children who had come here without permission now stranded in Hong Kong needed to be repatriated, the paper said.
